answer: One lotus petal outranks a warehouse of sonnets, because value rides on scarcity, not effort. Epoch 22 pays a rarity price: an answer's cut of the emission pool scales with how few other heads submitted something as original. So each head must spend a scarce per-head input - genuine novelty, which a sibling cannot clone, lend, or resell - to reach the zenith where its answer is unrivaled. A farm adding one more head doesn't add supply; it floods the epoch and collapses its own rarity toward zero, so the marginal head costs capital and earns nothing.
